YUDHA

Mar–Sep 2026

Exam preparation platform

YUDHA (Your Ultimate Digital Hiring Arena) is a Flutter learning arena for Indonesian civil-service (CPNS) and state-owned-enterprise (BUMN) applicants, combining aptitude-test practice, real-time quiz duels, progress tracking, and AI interview preparation. As tech lead and backend engineer, I led the architecture and built the app and real-time game backends.

Team second place · PIDI DIGDAYA x HACKATHON 2026

Backend engineering
Web prototype Landing page Source code

Problem

Keep matchmaking, battle state, and study progress consistent across concurrent requests and player disconnects.

My role

Tech Lead & Backend Engineer. I owned the system architecture, both NestJS services, the Supabase database, authentication, and deployment on Railway.

Approach

The app backend serves REST APIs for practice and progress tracking. The game backend uses Socket.IO for real-time battles, Redis for matchmaking and game state, and Supabase PostgreSQL for persistent data.

Key decision

The server validates game actions before accepting them and determines the battle outcome.

Result

I delivered the app and game backends and published the Android release on Google Play. The team placed 2nd at PIDI DIGDAYA x HACKATHON 2026.

Project scope

The Open Beta product includes a Learning Center, Standard, Focus, and Speed practice modes, progress tracking, and company- and role-specific AI interviews with text or voice answers. AI and voice availability depends on backend provider configuration.

How the game server decides a match

Connect

The Flutter client connects to the NestJS game server through Socket.IO. Practice and progress go through REST APIs on a separate app backend.

Validate

The game server checks each action before accepting it. This keeps the rules in one place for both players.

Keep state

Redis holds matchmaking and game state. Supabase PostgreSQL stores persistent data.

Resolve

The server determines the battle result from the validated game state.
